source.title: Deep learning generalization and the convex hull of training sets

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own convex-hull measurements and toy-network experiments, but does not test any listed claim version. It discusses generalization through a different geometric framing.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on random-label fitting, but reports no new random-label experiment. Its toy-network figures report training-set fit and decision-boundary shapes, not held-out test error; these do not test V2 as stated.
record.test_reason: The study measures convex-hull geometry and illustrates training fit and decision-boundary shapes. It reports no results testing V1–V8. In particular, its width experiments do not measure held-out error, and its argument about geometric extrapolation does not contradict V2's empirical width–test-error claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. For the examined datasets and representations, the authors conclude that classification requires moderate extrapolation beyond the training-set convex hull. They argue that over-parameterization may enable desirable boundary extensions and that training regime shapes those extensions, using polynomial and ReLU-network illustrations. They do not demonstrate that widening lowers held-out error.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies convex-hull geometry and toy decision-boundary behavior; it does not reproduce the methods in the listed original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: In the synthetic toy network, decision-boundary shapes vary with training regime; increasing neuron count increases outside-hull variation and the number of disjoint boundaries.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST and CIFAR-10 testing images lie outside the training-set convex hull in pixel and wavelet spaces; CIFAR-10 testing images also lie outside it in the two examined ResNet representations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out image classification can require geometric extrapolation beyond the training-set convex hull, including in learned representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing toy-network width improves training fit and changes boundary complexity; different training regimes produce different boundaries despite perfect training separation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model capacity and training regime affect decision-boundary extensions beyond the training-data convex hull.

fits_no_version.finding: The polynomial illustration assumes a desired outside-hull classification boundary and argues that increasing degree permits reshaping extensions while preserving the inside-hull shape.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional polynomial capacity can enable desired extrapolation, while selecting that extrapolation also requires an appropriate training regime.

record.problems: The image experiments report convex-hull geometry, not held-out classification error or comparisons among training recipes. Toy-network findings use a synthetic two-class task and plotted decision boundaries; the paper gives no numerical test-error results for those models. The paper states that pixel-space distances and locations are not always meaningful.

untested.parts: Joint evidence of random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy; the introduction only cites prior work.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance, local connectivity, and initialization effects.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization and its dependence on tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes, strengths and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; the geometric and training-fit observations themselves are supported by the supplied text. The paper critiques explanations based on geometric interpolation, which is distinct from achieving zero training error at an interpolation threshold.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Held-out test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold, on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Comparative test error for convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training–test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
